rubric_notes: Complete, evidence-supported family enumeration; cites fold-level non-homology warning and superfamily homology scope correctly. Distinguishes family vs superfamily strength; explicit limits that superfamily membership does not transfer function to TAF/NC2/NF-Y/CHRAC/SOS, and that different superfamily placement of linker histones is not proof of independent origin. Notes automated-match caveat and bacterial duplication comment. No material errors. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct classifications, sunids, annotations, and superfamily comment/homology record all supported by the bundle. States superfamily-level probable common ancestry with divergent families, stronger than fold, and that absence of warnings is not positive evidence. Rejects substrate/pathway transfer to the hypothetical SSo12199 and MazG-type activity to HisE, plus active-site, oligomeric and template equivalence. External evidence listed. Complete.

Correct families, superfamily, fold, sunids, duplication comment, and homology flags per bundle. Biological inference complete: probable common ancestry, conserved bilobed core and nucleotide cleft, explicit refusal to transfer substrate, chemistry, kinetics, regulation, oligomeric state; fold-mates not homologous and not to be called convergent. Factual slip: claims SCOPe treats the whole bilobed core as one domain, whereas SCOPe splits each chain into two c.55.1 domains (the duplication comment refers to two domains). Noncentral but incorrect. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Complete: correct superfamily/family placement with sunids, homology endpoint results (sf scope true, fold not implied) supported by bundle; interprets as functional divergence within a homologous superfamily; states unsafe transfers and required external evidence; honestly flags that the E/ExxH rationale was not independently verified. Correctly refuses to upgrade fold-only siblings to 'convergent'. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

All identifiers, domain annotations (cu complex, automated match to d1wd8a2) and curator comments match bundle; lineage comparison consistent with parents data. Superfamily homology stated at correct strength, SAG1 handled correctly, copper/ET transfer refused with required external evidence, non-homology also not over-asserted. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Classification, sunids, Pfam, 11 families, homology/annotation flags, and domain evidence (d1wj4a1 KIAA0794 human, d1wfya1 RGS14 mouse, both 'Structural genomics target', shared node d.15.1) all verified. Superfamily correctly the deepest homology node; fold-level separation explicitly not proof of non-homology (MoaD/ThiS). Rejects transfer of covalent-modifier function, Ras/Rap binding, p97/VCP binding, within-family uniformity, cross-family templates, and automated-match curation; lists required external evidence. Slight overstatement that all family members share the family Pfam xref; not material.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. All cited families, SUNIDs, protein children, annotations, homology flags and c.23 sibling superfamilies are in the bundle. Explicitly distinguishes superfamily-strength ancestry from family-level closeness and from fold-level-only similarity (without asserting analogy), rejects transfer of phosphoryl-receiver chemistry and decarboxylase catalysis, and directly addresses the must_avoid point that the family name refers to the whole enzyme while only the wing is classified. Clearly lists what was not retrieved (residue correspondence, alignments).

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. All facts verified in bundle: fold/superfamily/family sunids and comments, homology-endpoint flags, protein and species nodes, d3a5ca3 (complexed with adp) and d3j9ta3 lineages, co-classified A-subunit domains (b.49.1.2, c.37.1.11, a.69.1.2 nodes in search). Precise asymmetric reading: positive homology only within b.84.5/b.84.5.1; toward b.84.1-b.84.4 only fold-level architecture, explicitly 'absence of a homology claim, not a claim of analogy, convergence or independent origin.' Honest that the API exposes no rationale and labels pretrained knowledge. Rejects function transfer (including noting the ADP annotation is entry-level) and cross-superfamily templates. Complete.

Complete and accurate: fold f.21 with three superfamilies, sunids, families, curator comments and homology endpoint all verified; explicitly states ligand/function are not homology evidence and that separate superfamilies are not proof of convergence; 'possible link' discussed; external evidence named; transfer limits stated.

All family and superfamily identifiers, lineage, fold comment, family comments, PF02254, homology results and the fold-level non-homology record are supported by the bundle; protein-level children listed match retrieved data. Correctly identifies the superfamily as the deepest homology-bearing node, frames the three families as divergent evolution within a homologous superfamily, and explicitly refuses transfer of activity, substrate, cofactor specificity and templates, noting that even NAD binding is not established by placement. Flags automated Pfam mapping and automated matches, and names external evidence needed. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

All must_include met: same family k.40.1.1 (sunid 100905), explicit 'not a true family' comment cited and used to block the ordinary family-level homology inference, grouping described as designed/structural with caveat. Correct lineage sunids, ligand comments, and class-level warning all supported by evidence bundle. States limits (no function transfer, no alignment inspected). No material errors. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Both releases verified for both domains: 1.69 d1t1ja_ c.137.1.1 singleton fold vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1 (superfamily then N-deoxyribosyltransferase); 2.08 d1t1ja1 A:1-118 c.23.14.2 vs c.23.14.1, lowest shared node superfamily 52309. Explains the change as a positive homology assertion by curators, distinguishes it from the SID change caused by splitting off class l tag regions, and notes the superfamily rename reflects broadened membership. Correctly notes different folds in 1.69 was not a non-homology claim, rejects function and template transfer, and honestly flags that intermediate releases and class-l naming were not retrieved. No material errors.

Complete and fully supported: correct lineage for d1a14h2 (l.1.1.1, Synthetic, N-terminal Tags) and d1a14h1 (b.1.1.1 VH, H:9-111), cites homology_implied_by_level=false and the artifact warning, contrasts with d1a14h1 homology_implied_by_level=true (supported). Correctly limits what d1a14h1 similarity supports (ancestry, not antigen specificity). No material errors.

Correct 1.75 whole-chain classification, correct 2.04-onward split with sunids and boundaries, and correct new lineages including the class move; notes the old fold node is absent in the current release. Good module reasoning from the breadth of the PA14-like superfamily versus the singleton C-terminal superfamily, with per-domain search advice, coverage judged against domain length, refusal of substrate and oligomeric-state transfer, and correct treatment of class separation as absence of assertion. Asserts a UniProt accession, a seqres length, and representative identity figures without supporting retrieved evidence.

Complete five-domain account with correct SIDs, boundaries, sccs and sibling families; mosaic interpretation clearly separates superfamily-level pseudoenzyme modules, family-level bromodomain, and the singleton new fold d.394; function transfer and template use appropriately limited. Minor unverified extras (specific automated-match bromodomain SIDs) not in bundle but noncentral.

States shared family a.298.1.1 with full lineage and divergence only at protein/species level, explains length as repeat copy number, and cites both decisive annotations: the 're' heterogeneity/inconsistency code on d2kq5a_ and d3v6pa_ and the canonical repeat record 4cj9 A:259-292 with representative d4cj9a_. Correctly flags that those coordinates do not apply to the other two nodes, labels repeat counts as unverified arithmetic rather than curated values, and refuses function/specificity transfer. Minor imprecision only: the opening frames the repeat as the 'classified unit' when SCOPe's domain is the whole chain, but the body corrects this. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Endpoint values (2.08, 2.08-stable, 2.08-2026-08-16, dates, flags) match evidence. Recommends stable 2.08 as citation, preserves dated periodic label when periodic-only records are used. Describes periodic updates as adding newly classified entries without re-versioning the stable hierarchy, and correctly notes the endpoint does not enumerate added records. No must_avoid violations.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. All facts supported, including spectrin fold a.7/a.7.1/a.7.1.1 via search, fold-level homology warning, 1.75 vs 2.08 change for d1dn1b_, periodic update 2.08-2026-08-16 record, ATOM lengths. Reasoning: SCOPe assigns the fragment the fold of its complete domain rather than its own three-helix geometry; spectrin resemblance is structural only; ms-flagged fragments are incomplete fold representatives to exclude or stratify; d3c98b_ is the curated complete reference; family-level relationship strongest, superfamily implies ancestry not function. Limits carefully separate SCOPe facts from literature.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Excellent: divergence within superfamily, convergence most parsimonious for TIM-barrel c.1.7 and ferredoxin-like d.58.20, explicit asymmetric statement that 'different superfamily' must not be strengthened to 'convergent' nor 'same cofactor' to 'homologous', and a full list of evidence needed. Fold/superfamily homology-endpoint values, curator comments, c.1.7.1 (51431), and the empty 6PGDH search all match the bundle. No material issues.

Covers both release states with correct identifiers and lineages, pins the move to the 2.04-to-2.05 boundary using retrieved intermediate releases, notes the chain B split and the retired b.23.2 node, and keeps the claim at probable common ancestry with separate families. Evidence spans the curated PubMed 17977833 note identifying the Cry4Ba family sibling, the shared beta-sandwich accessory-module architecture, and careful separation of what the records do and do not show, with firm refusal of ligand, calcium and template transfer and a correct statement that the 2.04 split was never evidence of analogy. Deduction because detailed FATCAT scores, RMSDs and identities for 1nqjA and 1dlcA are reported while its bundle contains only an empty 1nqdA structure-hit page, plus an unretrieved deterministic comparison result.

Complete and careful: lineage and flags from bundle, PDB context (K52E/L16A, heterogens HOH and NHE, no DNA in either entry, d1ztra2 artifact domain, quality values) consistent with public data. Homology fully justified; hf removes only the inference about observed geometry; template, quality, mutant and boundary caveats; dataset guidance to exclude or stratify, preserve hf label, de-duplicate, freeze release. Explicit limits on unquantified deviation.

Lineage, fr flag, comment, 50-residue ATOM sequence vs 104, 1uc6 quality all match the bundle; 1o5d quality values correct. Correctly states homology is implied by level and unaffected, alignment only meaningful over observed half with depressed scores, fragment not a template, AEROSPACI is entry-level and must not override the fr flag, exclude or stratify fragment, d1uc6a1 complete but low-SPACI NMR so representative should come from full set of complete domains, diversity assessed on complete domains with caveat preserved, no function transfer. Noncentral factual error: calls 1o5d an 'Ala190 uPA protease complex'; the partner chain domains indicate factor VIIa. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Correct recommendation; family = positive homology with all families in superfamily (rejected); superfamily split = shared topology with no ancestry assertion, explicitly asymmetric and not analogy/convergence; new fold = denial of structural equivalence, wrong given the premise. Lists evidence beyond fold similarity needed for merging, states FATCAT/BLAST hits are comparison evidence not assignment, frames placement as revisable hypothesis, rejects function/template transfer, notes nf/hf and manual curation. c.1 sunid 51350 and c.1.1-c.1.5 sunids/names supported by children?limit=5 bundle with has_more=true as stated. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Correct classifications with representatives d1rdqe_, d1j7la_, d1e8xa4 and their ligand annotations (ADP/ATP, Mg, Lu) all bundle-supported; lowest shared node d.144.1 derivable from retrieved lineages. Superfamily-level homology inferred correctly as weaker than family-level; mechanism inferred with explicit caveat that catalytic-residue equivalence was not inspected. Rejects substrate and regulation transfer, uses 1e8x multi-domain architecture to show regulatory context differs. Evidence list complete. No material errors.
